text:
Predicates:
RosesOnTV(day, time) ::: On day at time, roses are given out on TV.
OnBachelor(x) ::: x is on the Bachelor.
PortraysLives(x) ::: x portrays the lives of real people.
RealityTV(x) ::: x is a reality TV show.
Show(x) ::: x is a TV show.
Premises:
∃day ∃time (day = monday ∧ time = 8pm ∧ RosesOnTV(day, time)) ::: On some Mondays at 8 pm, roses are given out on TV.
∀x (RosesOnTV(day, time) → OnBachelor(x)) ::: Every rose given out on TV is on the Bachelor.
∀x (OnBachelor(x) → PortraysLives(x)) ::: Everything on the Bachelor portrays the lives of real people.
∀x (PortraysLives(x) → RealityTV(x)) ::: All shows portraying the lives of real people are reality TV shows.
¬RealityTV(breakingBad) ::: Breaking Bad is not a reality TV show.
Conclusion:
RosesOnTV(monday, 8pm) ∧ Show(breakingBad) ::: Breaking Bad is a TV show in which roses are given out on Monday at 8 pm.
